title: Dominic and the Sigil
premise: Rosalind Thackeray survives in the memoryless valley by stealing recollections from travelers before the wards erase them, selling fragments to a black-market broker who may know more about the fallen border than he admits. When the wards collapse and the stars go dark, Rosalind learns the valley was a prison built around a stolen king—Dominic, whose true self is bound inside a sigil worn by the thing that usurped his crown. Gathering a found family of exiles, ward-breakers, and one very loyal talking crow, Rosalind must carry the king's scattered memories across a starless kingdom to the moonlit threshold where the sigil can be unbound. In the end, Rosalind chooses truth over the loyalty of the only family he's ever known, shattering the sigil at cost of his own stolen memories, and Dominic—restored but changed—offers him a new home not as a thief, but as the keeper of what everyone else forgot.
about_author: Isandro Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. They write fantasy about people who keep things—memories, promises, each other—and live somewhere it rains more than it should.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He works the border road, lifting memories from travelers before the valley's wards dissolve them, establishing his rules and his loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking a hunger for a past he cannot remember having.

chapters.title: Thirteen Coins
chapters.summary: Rosalind sells a stolen memory of a coronation to the broker Vess, who pays too much and asks too little. POV Rosalind. Beat: unease—the memory feels less like merchandise and more like a message.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: The sky goes black star by star; the valley's wards fail with a sound like breaking glass. POV Rosalind. Beat: terror and exhilaration as the world outside becomes visible for the first time.

chapters.title: What Walked Out of the Dark
chapters.summary: A wounded stranger collapses at Rosalind's door carrying a locked box and a talking crow named Quill. POV Rosalind. Beat: reluctant compassion overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Last Words
chapters.summary: The stranger dies whispering 'the thirteenth turn,' leaving Rosalind the box and a map inked in starlight. POV Rosalind. Beat: grief for someone he knew for a single night.

chapters.title: Vess Knows
chapters.summary: Rosalind confronts Vess, who reveals the valley is a prison built around a deposed king, Dominic, bound into a sigil. POV Rosalind. Beat: betrayal—his whole life has been someone else's containment strategy.

chapters.title: Quill Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: The crow reveals she served Dominic and can smell his scattered memories; she claims Rosalind's own forgotten past is tangled in them. POV Rosalind. Beat: vertigo—his identity is a question mark.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Rosalind crosses the dead border with Quill and the box; the valley tries to call him back through phantom voices. POV Rosalind. Beat: severance—burning the bridge behind him.

chapters.title: The Road of Unlit Lanterns
chapters.summary: In the starless countryside, villages worship the crown-thing out of fear. Rosalind meets Tam, a runaway ward-smith's apprentice. POV Rosalind. Beat: first spark of found family.

chapters.title: Tam's Broken Wards
chapters.summary: Tam confesses her master forged the original binding sigil and taught her its flaws before vanishing. POV Tam. Beat: guilt transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Memory Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Following Vess's ledger, they find a safehouse of exiles led by Odile, a disgraced royal cartographer. POV Rosalind. Beat: cautious hope among strangers who share his exile.

chapters.title: Odile's Map of Missing Things
chapters.summary: Odile has charted every place stars used to be; the first memory-shard lies beneath a drowned chapel. POV Odile. Beat: an old woman's redemption riding on a thief's shoulders.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Diving into floodwater, Rosalind retrieves a shard and experiences Dominic's coronation from inside the king's body. POV Rosalind. Beat: intimacy with a stranger's joy and dread.

chapters.title: The Crown's Hounds
chapters.summary: Sigil-bound hunters attack the safehouse; the exiles scatter, and Tam is captured. POV Tam. Beat: terror and defiance—she swallows the shard rather than surrender it.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Broker
chapters.summary: Rosalind trades his most precious stolen memory to Vess for Tam's location. POV Rosalind. Beat: sacrifice—he gives up a childhood he'd only just reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Gilded Prison
chapters.summary: Infiltrating the capital's pleasure-quarter prison, they free Tam, who has begun hearing the sigil speak through her. POV Tam. Beat: violation and resilience.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: From a rooftop, Rosalind sees the Regent in person and recognizes the face from Dominic's memories—identical, wrong. POV Rosalind. Beat: horror; the usurper wears the king like a coat.

chapters.title: Quill's Confession
chapters.summary: Quill admits she helped forge the binding, believing it would save Dominic from assassination. POV Quill (rendered through Rosalind). Beat: shame, forgiveness asked and half-given.

chapters.title: The Second Shard: The War Room
chapters.summary: Recovered from a general's tomb, this shard shows Dominic ordering the valley built—to hide something, not imprison someone. POV Rosalind. Beat: the mission's moral ground shifts.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Odile urges turning back; the shards suggest Dominic chose his binding. Rosalind refuses to stop. POV Odile. Beat: fracture lines in the found family.

chapters.title: The Moon Counts Thirteen
chapters.summary: An astronomer exile confirms the thirteenth turn falls in nineteen days, when the sigil becomes permanent. POV Rosalind. Beat: the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: Tam's Whispering Week
chapters.summary: The shard inside Tam speaks; she begins writing in a hand that isn't hers—Dominic's. POV Tam. Beat: fear becoming strange communion.

chapters.title: The Third Shard: The Lover's Letter
chapters.summary: Hidden in a lighthouse, a shard reveals Dominic bound himself to trap the crown-thing, which cannot survive without its host. POV Rosalind. Beat: devastating clarity—unbinding may kill them both.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Stole From Himself
chapters.summary: Quill recognizes a memory-shard's resonance in Rosalind: he is a fragment of Dominic, cut loose and made flesh. POV Rosalind. Beat: identity collapse—thief, keeper, or king?

chapters.title: The Family Decides
chapters.summary: The exiles vote on whether to continue knowing Rosalind might be a weapon or a decoy. POV Odile. Beat: belonging tested—they choose him anyway, which undoes him more than rejection would.

chapters.title: Storming the Ward-Smithy
chapters.summary: They raid the forge where the sigil was made to learn the unbinding rite; Tam's old master's ghost-notes reveal it requires a willing vessel. POV Tam. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Vess's True Face
chapters.summary: Vess is revealed as the crown-thing's herald, collecting Rosalind's sold memories to track the shards all along. POV Rosalind. Beat: the trap closes—every bargain was surveillance.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: A running battle under a moonless sky; Odile is gravely wounded holding the pass. POV Odile. Beat: love expressed as stubbornness—'go on, I'll catch up.'

chapters.title: The Tenth Turn
chapters.summary: With three turns left, they reach the moonlit threshold: a ruined observatory where the rite must occur. POV Rosalind. Beat: exhausted stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: The Crown Comes Calling
chapters.summary: The Regent offers Rosalind everything—identity, family, the valley reborn—if he delivers the shards willingly. POV Rosalind. Beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable.

chapters.title: Tam Chooses
chapters.summary: Tam volunteers as the vessel, arguing her ward-craft makes her the only one who can survive contact. POV Tam. Beat: courage as inheritance from a family that chose her.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Turn: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Vess's agents seize the shards; Quill is captured, and the rite's components fall into enemy hands. POV Rosalind. Beat: despair—the lowest point.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn: The Throne Room
chapters.summary: Dragged before the Regent, Rosalind speaks directly to Dominic inside the sigil, and something answers through the crown-thing's mouth. POV Rosalind. Beat: two prisoners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Quill's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Quill sacrifices herself to shatter the sigil's outer casing, buying one turn of vulnerability. POV Rosalind. Beat: grief as fuel—a small bird against a large darkness.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Tam channels the shards while Rosalind offers himself as the willing vessel; the unbinding tears both king and thief open. POV alternating Rosalind/Tam. Beat: climax—truth chosen over safety, over loyalty, over self.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Dawn
chapters.summary: The crown-thing unravels without its host; Dominic wakes mortal and diminished, and Rosalind remembers nothing of his stolen life. POV Dominic. Beat: hollow victory, tender and uncertain.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Forgotten Things
chapters.summary: Dominic, refusing the throne, establishes an archive of returned memories; the exiles become its founders. POV Dominic. Beat: rebuilding—family formalized into home.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Kept
chapters.summary: Sorting the returned memories, Rosalind finds one the magic couldn't reclaim: the night he chose to leave the valley. POV Rosalind. Beat: identity rebuilt from choice, not origin.

chapters.title: Stars Returning
chapters.summary: One year later, the first star rekindles above the observatory; the found family watches together. POV ensemble via Rosalind. Beat: quiet wonder—belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Rosalind writes their story into the archive's first book, titling it honestly: not the king's tale alone, but the thief who carried him home. POV Rosalind. Beat: resolution—truth told, kept, and shared.
